title: The drum kit
examples: Which part of the drum kit makes a sharp, cracking sound?
How do the different drums work together to keep the music going?
Can you show me how to keep a steady beat with a drumstick?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the drum kit.
The bass drum makes a deep, low sound.
The snare drum makes a sharp, rattling sound.
The hi-hat makes a steady, ticking sound.
Cymbals add bright, ringing sounds to the music.
Keeping the beat means playing steady rhythms.

faq.q: What is the main difference between the bass drum and the snare drum?
faq.a: The bass drum produces a very deep, low thud. The snare drum makes a higher, rattling sound.
asks: What sound does the big drum make?

faq.q: Does the hi-hat only make a ticking sound?
faq.a: The hi-hat can make different sounds depending on how you move the sticks. It is used for steady rhythm.
asks: Can I make other sounds on the hi-hat?

faq.q: Do I need to know all these drums to play?
faq.a: No, you can start by focusing on keeping a steady beat with just one drum. Practice makes it easier.

faq.q: What is 'keeping the beat' in music?
faq.a: It means playing sounds at a regular, even pace. It is the foundation of the rhythm in the music.

faq.q: Are the cymbals always used at the end of a song?
faq.a: Cymbals can be used throughout the song to add excitement. They are not only for the finish.

facts: The bass drum is typically the largest drum on the kit.
The snare drum has wires underneath that create the rattling sound.
The hi-hat is made of two metal cymbals that move together.
Keeping the beat is about maintaining a consistent tempo.

quiz.say: Which drum makes a deep, low thud sound?
quiz.why: The bass drum is designed to produce the lowest, deepest tones.

wrong.0: Cymbals produce a bright, ringing sound, not a deep bass sound.
wrong.2: The snare drum makes a sharp, rattling sound, not a deep thud.
wrong.3: The hi-hat makes a steady, ticking sound, which is different from a low thud.

quiz.say: If you want a steady, ticking sound, which part do you use?
quiz.why: The hi-hat is specifically used to create a consistent, rhythmic 'tss-tss' sound.

wrong.0: The snare drum is for sharp accents, not continuous ticking.
wrong.1: While cymbals can be steady, the hi-hat is the primary tool for that sound.
wrong.3: The bass drum is for big, spaced-out beats, not steady ticks.

quiz.say: A drummer needs to keep the music moving forward at a steady pace. Which skill is most important?
quiz.why: Keeping the beat means maintaining a consistent, steady rhythm throughout the piece.

wrong.0: Loud sounds are exciting, but the beat must remain steady regardless of volume.
wrong.2: Playing fast notes is good, but it does not guarantee a steady pace.
wrong.3: Using all the drums is fun, but rhythm is more about consistency.
